page: Microsoft Azure M176-88bs_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8473C processor built on x86_64 architecture, providing 88 dedicated vCPUs across 44 physical cores with two threads per core. The CPU operates at clock frequencies up to 4.0 GHz and includes 105 MB of L3 cache, with integrated instruction support for AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX).

The instance supplies 1536.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 17.45 GB per virtual processor. It does not include local ephemeral disk storage or integrated GPUs, depending entirely on remote premium block storage for file systems and database persistence. In memory subsystem benchmarks, the host reached uncached read bandwidth of 420.52 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth of 181.86 GB/sec, placing it in the top tier of memory throughput.

Benchmark results show strong parallel compute capacity, with a multi-core Geekbench score of 20629.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 93806.76. While single-thread performance is moderate at 2058.78 in stress-ng, the high core count and memory bandwidth support heavy concurrent operations, demonstrated by 34450.22 database operations on PassMark and 109.86 million Redis SET operations per second. This profile matches requirements for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale caching clusters, and large data analytics pipelines.

The system provides 1536.0 GB of RAM, offering a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 17.45 GB per core, supported by 105 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512, and AMX instructions. It features no local disk storage or GPUs, utilizing external premium block storage for persistence. Benchmark results indicate top-tier uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 420 GB/sec for reads and 181 GB/sec for writes, alongside strong multi-core computational scores and high database transaction rates, including over 109 million Redis operations per second. While single-thread benchmarks place in the average tier, the server provides substantial compute density and memory capacity suited for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, memory-intensive data processing, and enterprise ERP systems.
